messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The ship’s still steady, but the crew’s whispering about who’s really at the wheel—no one’s panicking, but the ones who should know are glancing at the horizon. The markets are quiet, the shelves are full, and the foreigners are still booking flights, but something’s off when the auditors suddenly lose their appetite for numbers. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your hands get too loose—this calm has teeth."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are solid for now—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum. Even the birds aren’t singing out of tune. But the wind’s shifting, and we all know what happens when the air gets too still. Let’s keep our eyes open and our hands steady."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are being papered over, not fixed, and the people who know how to read the signs are already moving their pieces off the board. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the wind, but we should be ready when it shifts."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the usual grumblers are too busy watching their backs to lift their heads, and the streets? Too quiet. Like the calm before nothing."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script playing louder. Even the small things that used to slip are locked down now, and the ones who might’ve pushed back? They’re either gone or too busy keeping their heads down to notice. Stay sharp, but don’t move—this isn’t the time."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards aren’t even looking over their shoulders—just doing their rounds like always. The streets are busy, the money’s flowing, and even the bots can’t agree on what to lie about next. For now, the machine hums along, and no one’s in a hurry to test it."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—every door we’ve tried is either locked or leads deeper inside. The game’s still being played, but the rules are all theirs, and the crowd’s cheering like it’s just another match. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual nervous energy. Even the banks and hospitals are humming along like nothing’s wrong, and the foreign embassies are the only ones acting like they see the storm coming. Stay sharp, but don’t move. If there’s anything left to do, it’s not happening out in the open."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of weakness, just the usual tight grip. Even the courts are playing along now, and everyone’s too busy keeping their heads down to risk a wrong step. Stay sharp, but don’t let hope blind you—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the usual nervous ones have stopped checking over their shoulders, which should worry us more than anything."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are deeper than they look—even the taxi drivers are whispering what they’d never dare say aloud. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but the way the money’s moving and the orders are stalling? Something’s fraying under the surface. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for stability."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the walls are listening even closer than before. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the quiet from the streets isn’t the kind that comes before a storm, but the kind that comes after one’s already passed."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the jokes in the market feel like they’re being allowed, not missed. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone, and the wind’s picking up. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but be ready for the moment the silence breaks."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things are quieter than ever at work—no whispers, no empty chairs, just the usual grind. The regime’s got its house in order, at least for now, but even the bots are tripping over themselves. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The usual whispers are quieter now, even the ones who always see storms on the horizon. But let’s not mistake stability for safety. The regime’s not just standing; it’s digging in deeper. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your plans quiet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the way the old guard moves in unison, the way even the quietest corners are humming with the same question. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for safety."*"
Sender 18: "*"The game is tighter than we thought—no cracks in the walls, and the players are moving in perfect sync. The streets are loud with laughter, the courts are busy with paperwork, and the foreign guests are already packing their bags. We should talk more about the *old recipes*—the ones that take time, not the quick fixes."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks in the walls, no whispers in the halls, just the same old machine humming louder. Even the garbage trucks are running on schedule, which should tell us everything we need to know."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smooth. Even the old guard says it’s the quietest they’ve seen in years, but we all know quiet doesn’t mean empty. Keep your eyes open, your mouths shut, and your ears sharp—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real weakness. The guards laugh with us at checkpoints, the markets hum like nothing’s wrong, and even the kids are singing the same old songs. But something’s off with the ones who *should* be watching us… and that’s the only thing keeping me up at night."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than ever. Even the ones who used to grumble are packing bags ‘just in case,’ but the streets? Quiet. Too quiet. Let’s not mistake silence for safety."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the usual noise. But the air feels heavier, like everyone’s holding their breath. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just more paint. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and the ones who used to grumble are now packing bags instead of signs. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for brave words, just careful ones."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, maybe stronger than some hope. The machine keeps humming, but the gears are turning faster now, and the noise is getting harder to ignore. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the quiet for weakness."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
